title: Gravity and Magnetism
seo_title: Year 4 Science: Gravity and Magnetism Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Identify that forces can be exerted by one object on another by direct contact or from a distance, such as gravity, magnetism and static electricity (summary of the Australian Curriculum v9.0 Science content description).
meta_desc: Free Year 4 science worksheets on non-contact forces: gravity, magnets that attract and repel, magnetic materials and static electricity. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Gravity, magnetism and static electricity are non-contact forces.
body_html:
How to think about it

Non-contact forces act from a distance, without touching.

  • Gravity pulls objects towards the centre of Earth. It keeps the Moon in orbit.
  • Magnets attract iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. Like poles repel; unlike poles attract.
  • Static electricity, such as a rubbed balloon, can attract light objects like paper and hair.
Example

North pole facing north pole. What happens?

like poles

Answer: they repel

Example

Will a magnet pick up an aluminium can?

aluminium is not a magnetic metal

Answer: no

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all metals are magnetic (aluminium, copper and gold are not).
  • Thinking heavier objects always fall much faster.
  • Thinking gravity only works on Earth.

faq.a: Magnets attract iron, steel, nickel and cobalt. They do not attract aluminium, copper, gold, plastic, wood or glass.

faq.q: Why is gravity called a non-contact force?
faq.a: Gravity pulls objects towards Earth without touching them. It even pulls on the Moon from far away.
It is an electric charge that builds up when some materials are rubbed together. It can make hair stand up and balloons stick to walls.
